privacy.lastUpdated: last updated 2026-07-23 · plain english, no dark patterns.
privacy.storeBody1: When you sign in with Google, we store your email, display name, and profile photo URL — nothing else from your Google account. Everything else in Ignia is stuff you enter yourself: weight, calories, protein, dates, body measurements, meal labels, training toggles, and custom meal presets.
privacy.storeBody2: All of this is stored in Google Cloud Firestore, scoped to your user ID. No one else — including us — can read it without your Google login.
privacy.healthBody: If you connect Apple Health (iOS) or Health Connect (Android), Ignia reads only the metrics you approve — weight, sleep, water, steps and active energy — and writes back the weight, sleep, water, body fat, nutrition and workouts you log, so the two stay in sync. Steps and active energy are read-only: your phone or watch measures them and Ignia never writes them back. This exchange happens on your device between Ignia and the system health store. Health data is used solely to keep your own log up to date: we never use it for advertising, never sell it, never share it with any third party, and never use it to train models. You can revoke access at any time in iOS Settings → Privacy & Security → Health, or in the Health Connect app on Android, and revoking it does not delete anything already saved in your Ignia log. Deleting your account removes that data along with everything else.
privacy.geminiHeading: What we send to Google's Gemini AI
privacy.geminiIntro: Two features send data to Google's Gemini AI:
privacy.geminiPhoto: Photo-to-Macros: the meal photo you take is sent to Gemini 2.0 Flash for calorie + protein estimation. Photos are processed in-flight and not retained by us. Google's API retention policy applies — see Gemini API terms.
privacy.geminiCoach: AI Coach consultations: your question, 14-day log summary, profile fields (age, sex, height, activity level, pace), and current TDEE are sent to Gemini as context for each consultation. Your raw email, name, or photo are never included.
privacy.dontSell: We don't sell your data to anyone.
privacy.dontTrain: We don't use your data to train any AI model.
privacy.dontShare: We don't share your data with anyone outside our list of sub-processors: Google Cloud / Firebase (hosting, auth, Firestore, FCM), Google Gemini API (photo analysis + AI coach), Resend (transactional email — your address, so we can send password resets, the welcome email, and the weekly digest), Stripe (payments only — if you subscribe), and Sentry (crash reports, scrubbed of personal content). We don't use third-party analytics or ad trackers. We do keep a small first-party usage counter — one document per person per day, holding only how many times things like a meal being logged, or the app being opened, happened. It records no meal names, no macros, no photos and no free text, it lives in your own account, and it is deleted with it.
privacy.callExport: Export: download all your logs as CSV from the dashboard at any time.
privacy.callFullExport: Full JSON export: every profile field, log, preset, weight, measurement, report, and quota record we hold for you — portable format for GDPR Art. 20 requests.
privacy.callDelete: Delete: use the button below to permanently erase your account and every log, preset, weight, measurement, and report tied to it. This is irreversible.
privacy.deleteStepsIntro: You can delete your Ignia account and everything in it yourself, at any time. You don't need to ask us, and we don't ask why.
privacy.deleteStepsApp: In the iOS app: Settings → Delete account, then type delete to confirm.
privacy.deleteStepsWeb: On the web: sign in, come back to this page, and use the delete account box at the bottom.
privacy.deleteStepsNoAccess: If you can't sign in — you lost access to the account, or you already removed the app — email support@ignia.fit from the address you signed up with. We'll delete it for you, within 30 days and usually much sooner.
privacy.deleteWhat: What gets deleted: your profile, every log, preset, custom food, weight, measurement, workout, and report, plus the sign-in record itself. Deleting the account also revokes Sign in with Apple. It is immediate and irreversible — there is no recovery window and no archived copy we can restore from.
privacy.deleteRetention: What briefly remains: routine encrypted Firestore backups can still hold a copy for up to 30 days, as part of standard Google Cloud operation. They are not human-accessible, they are never used to repopulate a deleted account, and they age out automatically. After that, nothing of yours is left.
privacy.gdprBody: If you live in the European Economic Area, the UK, or Switzerland, the General Data Protection Regulation applies to your data. You can exercise the following rights at any time — email us or use the in-app controls described in "what you can do" above.
privacy.gdprAccess: Access — ask for a copy of the personal data we hold about you.
privacy.gdprRectify: Rectification — correct any inaccurate or incomplete data through the app or by emailing us.
privacy.gdprErase: Erasure — delete your account and all associated data (Privacy → Delete account).
privacy.gdprPortable: Portability — export your logs as CSV from Dashboard → Export.
privacy.gdprRestrict: Restriction — ask us to stop processing your data while a dispute is resolved.
privacy.gdprObject: Objection — object to any processing you believe isn't legitimate.
privacy.ccpaBody: If you live in California, the CCPA and CPRA apply. We do not sell or share your personal information with third parties for cross-context behavioural advertising, full stop. You have the right to know what personal data we hold, to request deletion, and to appeal any denial. Use the same export / delete controls above, or email us directly.
privacy.jurisdictionBody: The data controller for Ignia is Bermudez Systems LLC, a Wyoming limited liability company. Preferred contact for data-subject requests is email: support@ignia.fit. If you can't use email, open a public issue at our GitHub issue tracker or use the in-app Settings → Feedback button. We respond within 30 days as required by GDPR. This policy and your use of Ignia are governed by the laws of the operator's home jurisdiction (Puerto Rico, United States), without regard to conflict-of-law principles.
privacy.medicalBody: Ignia is not a medical device, and the AI coach is not a dietician. Nothing in the app is medical advice. If you're doing anything clinically meaningful — a cut below 1,500 kcal, weight loss of more than 1% body weight per week, or eating for a medical condition — talk to a real human doctor or RD first.

terms.lastUpdated: last updated 2026-07-07 · short, because you shouldn't need a lawyer to read this.
terms.dealBody: Ignia is a calorie, protein, and weight tracker with an AI coach. By signing in, you agree to use it as intended — a personal logging tool — and not to abuse it (scraping, reverse-engineering the webhook, attempting to access other users' data, etc).
terms.medBody: The numbers this app shows (TDEE, target, envelope, coach replies) are estimates, not prescriptions. The AI coach is a language model trained on public text — treat it like a knowledgeable friend who could be wrong, not a doctor or dietitian. Talk to a real human professional before making significant dietary changes, especially if you have a medical condition, are pregnant, under 18, or recovering from an eating disorder.
terms.dataBody: You own your data. You can export it as CSV or delete your account at any time from the privacy page. We keep backups for up to 30 days as part of standard Google Cloud Firestore operations; these are not human-accessible and are auto-purged.
terms.availBody: Ignia runs on Google Cloud. We do our best to keep it up, but don't guarantee uptime. We may change features, pricing, or these terms — when we do, the footer's "last updated" date will change and meaningful changes will be announced in-app.
terms.liabilityBody: Ignia is provided "as is" and "as available," without warranties of any kind, express or implied, including merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, and non-infringement. We're not liable for decisions you make based on its output, for lost data, or for any indirect, incidental, or consequential harm from using the app. To the maximum extent allowed by law, our total liability to you is capped at whatever you've paid us in the last 12 months (which for most users is zero).
terms.arbBody: Please read this carefully — it affects your legal rights. If we have a dispute we can't resolve by email, you and the developer agree to resolve it through binding individual arbitration rather than in court, except that either of us may bring an eligible claim in small-claims court. You and the developer waive the right to a jury trial and the right to bring or participate in a class action or class-wide arbitration — disputes are handled only on an individual basis. Arbitration will be administered under the consumer rules of a recognized provider such as AAA or JAMS. You may opt out of this arbitration agreement within 30 days of first accepting these terms by emailing support@ignia.fit with the subject "Arbitration opt-out." If any part of this section is unenforceable, the rest still applies, except a court (not an arbitrator) decides any claim that cannot be waived.

These terms are governed by the laws of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico and applicable U.S. federal law, without regard to conflict-of-laws rules. Ignia is offered only in the United States and Puerto Rico and is not directed to users in the EU, UK, or EEA.
terms.subsBody: Ignia has no paid plans today. Every feature is free, there is nothing to purchase, and no payment details are collected. This section describes how subscriptions would work if and when they are ever offered, and takes effect only from that point onward. Pro would be offered monthly or annually via Stripe, with the price shown on the subscribe card before you are charged. Plans would auto-renew at the end of each billing cycle, and could be cancelled at any time from Settings, with cancellation taking effect at the end of the current paid period. A receipt would be emailed for every renewal. Any price change would be announced in-app, and an existing price honoured through the current term.

EU / UK / Switzerland: If you're a consumer in the EU, UK, or Switzerland, you have a 14-day statutory right of withdrawal from the date of your first subscription charge. To exercise it, email support@ignia.fit within 14 days with the email address on your account — we'll issue a full refund, no questions asked.

Everywhere else: We don't offer automatic refunds for partial billing periods, but if something feels wrong — a forgotten renewal you didn't intend, a feature that didn't work for you, a platform issue on our end — email us and we'll make it right. The 7-day free trial gives you a no-charge window to confirm Ignia is for you before any money moves.

Chargebacks: please email us before filing a chargeback; we can almost always resolve it faster than Stripe can.

faq.pageTitle: Macro & calorie FAQ — answers without the fluff | Ignia
faq.title: Macros, calories, and fat loss — straight answers.
faq.intro: Common questions from the people who actually use Ignia. Short, practical, no clickbait.
faq.ctaTitle: Want a target you can act on today?
faq.ctaBody: Use the free calculator. No sign-up required.

items.q: How many calories should I eat to lose weight?
items.a: A reasonable starting point is your bodyweight in pounds × 11 for fat loss. So a 180 lb person aiming to drop fat lands around 1,980 kcal/day. This works for most people because it builds in a ~500 kcal/day deficit off a typical maintenance estimate. Track for two weeks and adjust based on actual weight change — the formula is the seed, your weight trend is the truth.

items.q: How much protein do I really need?
items.a: 0.7 to 1.0 grams per pound of bodyweight. The lower end is fine for general health; the upper end matters when you're in a calorie deficit because protein protects lean mass while you lose fat. A 180 lb person targeting fat loss should aim for ~180 g/day.

items.q: Do I need to track carbs and fat?
items.a: Not strictly. If you hit your calorie ceiling and your protein floor, the carb/fat split takes care of itself for most people. Track them later if you're chasing performance gains, optimizing for satiety, or have a specific medical reason.

items.q: Why isn't the scale moving even though I'm in a deficit?
items.a: Three usual suspects: (1) you're under-counting calories — most people are off by 200-500 kcal/day, (2) water retention is masking real fat loss for 1-3 weeks, especially after a hard workout or salty meal, (3) you've been at it less than two weeks. Weight loss isn't linear; the trend over a 2-3 week window is what matters, not any single morning.

Almost never. A loss of 0.5-1% of bodyweight per week is the sweet spot — fast enough to see progress, slow enough to keep muscle and stay sane. Cutting harder than 1.5%/week tanks training quality and adherence, and the scale catches up the moment you eat normally for two days.

items.q: How accurate is a bodyweight-based calorie estimate?
items.a: Within ~10-15% for the average person. Two people at 180 lb can have maintenance calories that differ by 300+ kcal because of activity level, lean mass, and metabolic adaptation. The calculator gets you started; once you've logged 14 days, Ignia switches to a measured TDEE based on your actual weight trend, which is much more accurate.

items.q: Do I need to weigh my food to track macros?
items.a: For the first few weeks, yes — if you want the numbers to mean anything. After 1-2 months you'll have a calibrated eyeball for common portions and can switch to estimating with reasonable accuracy. Cheap kitchen scale: $15. Best fitness investment you'll make.

A single 1,000 kcal surplus day undoes about 1.5 days of a moderate deficit — annoying but recoverable. The actual problem with cheat days is they often roll into cheat weekends. Build in 1-2 high-calorie meals per week instead of one full day off the rails. The math is identical, the psychology is gentler.

items.q: Should I eat back my exercise calories?
items.a: Mostly no. Fitness trackers over-estimate burn by 20-50%, and eating back the inflated number erases your deficit. Pick a sustainable daily calorie target and treat exercise as separate — fuel performance, build the habit, but don't use it as a calorie debit card.

items.q: Does Ignia track carbs and fat?
items.a: Yes — every entry has carb and fat fields, and they show on your day. What Ignia does not do is set targets for them. For the audience we built this for — lifters, people in a cut, anyone doing a recomp — calories and protein are the two numbers that move the needle, so those are the two that get rings and a daily goal. Carbs and fat are there when you want them, without turning every meal into four decisions.

items.q: Is this a replacement for a dietitian?
items.a: No. The calculator and the app give you a starting target and a way to track adherence. If you're managing a medical condition (diabetes, kidney issues, eating disorder history, pregnancy), work with a registered dietitian. The math is general; their advice is specific to you.

items.q: What happens after I sign up?
items.a: Two-question onboarding (current weight, goal), then you're logging meals against your targets in under 30 seconds. Everything is free — full history, barcode scanning, photo logging, the fasting timer and targets that adapt to your own weight trend. There is no paid tier and nothing to upgrade to.
